methodology:
Duxton Broadacre Farms is in active strategic transition (2024-2025) — divesting NSW assets and building a Northern Australia (NT + WA) presence. Recent transactions provide useful internal benchmarks:
- Timberscombe (8,432 ha at West Wyalong NSW) sold November 2024 for A$70M = ~A$3,360/acre — the highest-quality NSW Riverina property
- Cowaribin (940 ha) sold August 2024 for A$6M = ~A$2,580/acre

4-row breakdown:
- Forbes District NSW (18.5K ac): 3 named properties (Walla Wallah, Yarranlea, West Plains) — Central West NSW with substantial water entitlements
- Cowaribin / Kentucky / Merriment cluster (6K ac NSW Western Riverina)
- Sunraysia dried-grape vineyards (Euston + Wemen): 1,491 ac specialty
- Northern Territory + WA transition (38K ac): newer/smaller portfolio at lower per-acre

FY25 (Jun 2025) was loss-making with negative EBITDA from drought + weak grain prices. Land FMV is structurally less volatile than earnings.
